title: A thousand years ago, this was the most dazzling city in Europe.

post.caption: Córdoba, capital of al-Andalus: the Great Mosque, the caliphate of 929, and the cathedral built inside it. Images: public domain / CC0.

beats.text: A thousand years ago, this was the most dazzling city in Europe.
In the 780s, a prince who had escaped a massacre of his family in Syria began a great mosque in Córdoba.
beats.say: In the seven-eighties, a prince who had escaped a massacre of his family in Syria began a great mosque in Córdoba.

beats.text: His heirs kept enlarging it: a forest of more than eight hundred columns under red and white arches.
In 929 Abd al-Rahman the Third declared himself caliph, defying Baghdad. Envoys came from Byzantium and the German emperor.
beats.say: In nine twenty-nine Abd al-Rahman the Third declared himself caliph, defying Baghdad. Envoys came from Byzantium and the German emperor.

beats.text: Outside the city he built a whole palace town: Medina Azahara.
His son's library was said to hold four hundred thousand books. Historians doubt the number, but not the fame.
Then civil war tore the caliphate apart. In 1031 it shattered into rival little kingdoms.
beats.say: Then civil war tore the caliphate apart. In ten thirty-one it shattered into rival little kingdoms.

beats.text: Christian Castile took Córdoba in 1236. Three centuries later, a cathedral was built right in the middle of the mosque.
beats.say: Christian Castile took Córdoba in twelve thirty-six. Three centuries later, a cathedral was built right in the middle of the mosque.

beats.text: Mosque or cathedral? Córdoba still argues about what to call it.
